title: Review: Protein secretion and the endomembrane system; Cell surface area and size limits; Gas exchange surfaces and SA:V in organisms; Membrane structure (fluid mosaic)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE03#t2 term and clue written for the game; MB01a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE03#t1 term and clue written for the game; MB01a#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE03#N.11b, EX01a#N.10, MB01a#N.3b, MB06#N.12, EX01a#N.11a, MB01a#N.10b, MB06#N.9, MB06#N.5, MB06#N.3b. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Glycoproteins
items.clue: Molecules made when carbohydrate chains are added to polypeptides

items.label: Phospholipid
items.clue: Molecule with a charged, water-loving head and two non-polar fatty acid tails.

items.label: Exocytosis
items.clue: Vesicles fuse with the plasma membrane, releasing their contents outside the cell

items.label: Hydrophobic
items.clue: Describes non-polar parts, such as fatty acid tails, that are kept away from water.

questions.stem: Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that can break down proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and polysaccharides. Which statement best describes the role of the lysosome's membrane in the cell?

options.text: It stores the enzymes in an inactive form until they are released to digest material in the cytosol.
It protects the enzymes from being used up, as each enzyme molecule can act just once.
It supplies the enzymes with the food and oxygen that they need in order to stay alive.
It keeps the enzymes apart from the cell's own molecules, so they digest only material delivered to them.

questions.stem: Use the data on the mouse, human and elephant. Which statement is supported by the data?

options.text: The mouse uses more energy each day than the elephant, since its rate per kg is far higher.
Each kg of body uses energy at about the same rate in all three, so total use is proportional to mass.
Each kg of mouse uses energy about 13 times as fast as each kg of elephant.
The elephant has the highest rate per kg, because its greater surface area loses more heat.

questions.explanation: 720 ÷ 56 ≈ 13. The small mouse has a high SA:V, loses heat fast per kg, and so respires fast per kg.

questions.stem: In a plasma membrane, the phosphate heads of the phospholipids face the cytosol and the extracellular fluid, and the fatty acid tails face each other in the interior of the membrane. Which statement best explains this arrangement?

options.text: The tails are the polar part of each molecule, and polar groups strongly attract one another.
The cell places each phospholipid so that its tail is shielded from the surrounding water.
The heads are polar and interact with water, while the nonpolar tails are kept away from it.
The heads are too large to fit inside the membrane, so the thin tails pack there instead.

questions.stem: A spherical single-celled organism grows from a radius of 10 µm to a radius of 30 µm, keeping its shape. Which prediction is best supported?

options.text: Its SA:V rises to three times the original, so each unit of volume is better supplied.
Its SA:V is unchanged, because its shape has not changed.
Its surface grows ninefold, so supply now easily exceeds its larger needs.
Its SA:V falls to one third, so less surface serves each unit of volume.

questions.explanation: SA:V goes from 0.30 to 0.10 µm⁻¹. Demand grows × 27; supply surface only × 9.

questions.stem: An amoeba gets all its oxygen by diffusion across its cell-surface membrane. Why could a mouse not get enough oxygen by diffusion across its body surface alone?

options.text: A mouse has a smaller total surface area than an amoeba, so less oxygen can cross into its body.
A mouse has a much lower SA:V, and most of its cells lie too far from its surface for diffusion to supply them.
A mouse's cells are each much larger than an amoeba's cell, so every cell needs more oxygen than diffusion delivers.
Diffusion of oxygen can happen only in water, so a mouse on land cannot use it at any surface.

questions.stem: According to the fluid mosaic model, which statement correctly describes the plasma membrane of a vertebrate animal cell?

options.text: Proteins, cholesterol, glycoproteins and glycolipids sit among the phospholipids and move sideways.
Proteins, cholesterol and other components move into and out of the cell, which makes the membrane fluid.
Proteins form two continuous layers that coat the phospholipids, holding the other parts in place.
Proteins, cholesterol and glycolipids are embedded in a single layer of phospholipids around the cell.

questions.explanation: The framework is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins, cholesterol, glycoproteins and glycolipids embedded in it. All of them can move sideways within the membrane.

questions.stem: Shrews are among the smallest mammals. Like larger mammals, they keep their body temperature nearly constant. A shrew must eat much more food per gram of its body mass each day than a deer does. Which statement best explains this difference?

options.text: A shrew's cells are much smaller than a deer's, so each has a higher SA:V and needs more food per gram.
A shrew's small body can store only a little heat, so it must eat often to refill that store.
A shrew uses more energy in total each day than a deer does, because its rate per gram of body mass is higher.
A shrew has a higher SA:V, so it loses heat faster per gram and needs more energy per gram to replace it.

questions.stem: A hypothetical single-celled organism has the shape of a rectangular solid, 20 μm long, 10 μm high and 10 μm wide. What is the cell's surface area-to-volume ratio?
A hypothetical spherical cell grows until its radius has doubled, keeping the same shape. What happens to its SA/V?

options.text: It doubles, because a bigger cell has more membrane.
It stays the same, because surface area and volume increase together.
It halves: surface area becomes 4 times larger, volume 8 times.
It falls to a quarter, because surface area depends on the square of the radius.

questions.explanation: Radius × 2: area × 2² = 4, volume × 2³ = 8, so SA/V × 4/8 = one half.
